title: Skeletal form is largely a diagram of mechanical stress

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Skeletal form is largely a diagram of mechanical stress

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Skeletal form, as produced by growth, is to a very large extent determined by mechanical stress: material is laid down along the lines of stress so as to avoid shear, from the trabeculae within each bone to the arrangement of the bones in the whole skeleton.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. XVI: On Form and Mechanical Efficiency

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Let us not press either argument or hypothesis too far: but be content to see that skeletal form, as brought about by growth, is to a very large extent determined by mechanical considerations, and tends to manifest itself as a diagram, or reflected image, of mechanical stress.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter XVI, “On Form and Mechanical Efficiency”; topic “Skeletal form as a diagram of stress”. Scope: vertebrate skeletons, from bone microstructure to whole-skeleton architecture

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch16-16: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.52

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Stress-form alignment is measurable after substantial choices, and public scans support many case studies. The breadth, causal language and circular dependence of stress on geometry prevent a clean whole-skeleton resolution.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Across scales, compare skeletal orientations and material distribution with principal stresses predicted under habitual loading, and quantify variance explained relative to developmental, phylogenetic and neutral alternatives.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Observed form influences calculated stress, creating circularity.

“Very large extent” has no numerical threshold.

Habitual loads are rarely observed.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Pieces of the claim, especially trabecular and long-bone alignment, can be tested with existing scans. The sentence itself sums every level of the skeleton into one unquantified tendency. Those datasets can support or weaken local versions and leave the global claim without a single confirming or refuting result.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Quantify, from trabeculae up to whole-skeleton layout, the fraction of bony material aligned with computed principal stresses, and set a threshold for 'a very large extent'. The claim would be supported only if that fraction is high at both scales across vertebrates; alignment confined to a few bones, or a low fraction once loads are fixed in advance, would refute the global wording.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Stress maps and the skeleton that is supposed to diagram them are often inferred from the same geometry.

The phrase 'a very large extent' has no numerical cutoff, so many partial alignments count as success.
